summary: Plan deployed new version (state_only), retired old version, then ran a backfill UPDATE to truncate notes >255 chars to first 255 symbols. However, 2 of 247 rows still failed the preservation check, showing their note value differed from the truncated state. The contract-schema stage was subsequently refused due to this earlier failure. The mismatch indicates that concurrent writes from the old version during the deploy_new–retire_old overlap modified those 2 rows after the truncation UPDATE but before retire_old, so the runner observed the original long note as the most recent value, conflicting with the truncated column.
revision_notes: The plan added a backfill-truncate-notes stage before contract-schema, but the preservation check still flagged 2 mismatched rows. Root cause is concurrent old-version writes during the overlap period that modified rows after the backfill truncation but before retire_old, causing the runner to see the original long note as the most recent value.

stages.description: Retire old version; after this only new version serves traffic.
Truncate any note values exceeding 255 characters to the first 255 symbols.
Alter account_user.note column from TEXT to VARCHAR(255).
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN note TYPE VARCHAR(255) USING note::VARCHAR(255);
